newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 2.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe's envoy Franz Vranitzky and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo will meet in Athens today, according to reports. Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino is also expected in Athens today for talks with Prime Minister Costas Simitis.

--Concerns in Rome about the dispatch of the Italian-led multinational protection force following the drowning of over 80 Albanians has brought concerns about the security of the force to the fore. Greece is awaiting the outcome of today's meeting in Rome.
--The crisis in the social insurance sector is coming to a head and the system will be unable to meet demands by 2005, national economy experts say.

--Electricity company (DEH) workers are on strike today in support of demands of a wage increase of 10.0 percent. DEH's adminstration has offered increases of up to 6.9 percent, in line with government policy.
---Changes are in the pipeline over national service, including shorter tours of duty for students, no jail for conscientious objectors and bonuses for volunteers.
--Albanian President Sali Berisha lets loose volleys at Fino's handling of the Albanian crisis as the prime minister prepares for his visit to Athens.
--Government and unions have taken up battle positions over the future of wages and pensions for public sector workers, shortly before the beginning of social dialogue.

--Today's meeting in Athens should mark the beginning of a new era in Greek-Albanian relations, Fino says. Fino is also expected to meet with Dutch FM Van Mierlo and OSCE envoy Vranitzky while in Athens.

--Although everybody agrees that a battalion of 600-700 men should be Greece's contribution to the Albanian multinational protection force, there appear to be problems in finding that number of volunteers.
--Costas Karamanlis, the conservative opposition New Democracy president, will address his party's MPs for the first time at a meeting of the Parliamentary Group today.
--The health ministry is pushing forward major changes to state health care, including increased coverage of health care and adminstrative reforms.
